<description>
**Problem:** Block index ordering is used by chain selection and `CheckBlockIndex()`. The work comparator is defined out of line and can compare the same chain work twice.
`CheckBlockIndex()` is enabled by default on regtest, including functional tests, but disabled by default on mainnet.

**Fix:** Inline the block-index comparators, compare the work-ordering key with `std::tie`, and use one three-way comparison per 32-bit word in `arith_uint256`.

| Compiler     | Synthetic 256-bit work comparisons | CheckBlockIndex |
|--------------|-----------------------------------:|----------------:|
| GCC 15.0.1   |                              6.51× |           1.62× |
| Clang 22.0.0 |                              6.80× |           1.39× |
</description>

[2026-11-13] c:6853278094 comment by l0rinc (member):
Thanks @sedited, the benchmarks & tests have served their purpose (to make absolutely sure I didn't accidentally change anything else), but are excessive to keep.
I removed most of them, replaced the sorting tests with direct checks, and added one for most-significant-word precedence.
I kept `cblockindex_comparator` to pin the expected ordering before the refactors, since chain selection and `CheckBlockIndex()` share the comparator and need an independent check of its behavior.
</new_statements>
